sentences.zh: 2025年临近，你是不是也觉得有点精疲力竭？

sentences.en: Put your to-do list on pause and join me for an evening of science, storytelling, and connection.
sentences.zh: 暂时放下你的待办清单，和我一起享受一个充满科学、故事与连结的夜晚。

sentences.zh: 11月22日，我将把“隐藏的大脑”感知之旅带到洛杉矶的奥菲姆剧院。

sentences.zh: 我将分享该节目第一个十年中的七个关键心理学见解。

sentences.zh: 我很高兴地宣布，我们正在为2026年巡演增加更多场次。

sentences.zh: 我将于3月21日前往费城，3月25日前往纽约市。

sentences.zh: 要购买我们2026年演出的门票，请访问 hiddenbrain.org 斜杠 tour 并使用促销代码 BRAIN。

sentences.en: I hope to see you there.

sentences.en: And here's today's show.
sentences.zh: 这里是今天的节目。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedant.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When we are facing struggles with our thoughts or our emotions, many of us turn first to medication or therapy as solutions.
sentences.zh: 当我们面对思想或情感上的挣扎时，我们许多人首先转向药物或治疗作为解决方案。

sentences.en: The share of American adults reporting they took prescription drugs for mental health conditions stood at 19% in 2022.
sentences.zh: 根据凯撒家庭基金会对政府数据的分析，2022年报告因心理健康问题服用处方药的美国成年人比例为19%。

sentences.en: That's according to an analysis of government data by the Kaiser Family Foundation.
sentences.zh: 这是根据凯撒家庭基金会对政府数据的分析得出的。

sentences.en: For many people, such measures are enormously helpful, even essential.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这些措施非常有帮助，甚至是必不可少的。

sentences.en: At the same time, it may be the case that we are overlooking a potential source of relief that is literally right outside our door.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们可能忽视了一个潜在的慰藉来源，它字面意思上就在我们的门外。

sentences.en: This remedy costs nothing, has no known side effects, and is often delightfully pleasant.
sentences.zh: 这个疗法不花钱，没有已知副作用，而且通常令人心旷神怡。

sentences.en: We are talking about spending time in nature.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是在大自然中度过时间。

sentences.en: The capacity of the natural world to soothe and refresh our sensibilities has been known for centuries.
sentences.zh: 大自然抚慰和刷新我们感官的能力已经为人所知数个世纪了。

sentences.en: But it's only recently that scientists have begun to identify exactly what it is about the outdoors that has such a powerful effect on our moods and our minds.
sentences.zh: 但直到最近，科学家们才开始准确确定户外究竟是什么对我们的情绪和心灵产生了如此强大的影响。

sentences.en: Nature is filled with curved edges, and one thing that we found in our research is that people really like images that have more curved edges, even built images.
sentences.zh: 大自然充满了圆润的边缘，我们在研究中发现的一件事是，人们真的很喜欢有更多圆润边缘的图像，甚至是人造图像。

sentences.en: So images of architectural scenes that don't have any nature in them, if the architecture has more curved edges, people tend to like that architecture more.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于没有任何自然景观的建筑场景图像，如果建筑有更多圆润的边缘，人们往往会更喜欢这种建筑。

sentences.en: If you struggle with the ability to think clearly, to focus your attention, to control maladaptive behaviors,
sentences.zh: 如果你在清晰思考、集中注意力、控制适应不良行为方面感到挣扎，

sentences.en: this episode and a companion story on Hidden Brain Plus are definitely for you.
sentences.zh: 这一集以及“隐藏的大脑普拉斯”上的配套故事绝对适合你。

sentences.en: Why Nature is Good Medicine, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 为什么大自然是良药，本周“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Many of us enjoy an occasional stroll in the park or a hike in the woods.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都喜欢偶尔在公园散步或在树林里徒步。

sentences.en: It feels good to see beautiful trees, to hear birds sing, and to breathe fresh air.
sentences.zh: 看到美丽的树木，听到小鸟歌唱，呼吸新鲜空气，感觉真好。

sentences.en: But might nature offer more than a fleeting respite from our time-pressured, harried lives?
sentences.zh: 但大自然是否能提供超越我们时间紧迫、忙碌生活的短暂喘息？

sentences.en: At the University of Chicago, psychologist Mark Berman studies how spending time in nature can help our minds.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥大学，心理学家马克·伯曼研究在大自然中度过时间如何帮助我们的心灵。

sentences.en: Mark Berman, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 马克·伯曼，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on the show.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我参加节目。

sentences.en: I want to start with a few examples of the phenomenon you've been studying, Mark.
sentences.zh: 马克，我想从你一直在研究的现象的几个例子开始。

sentences.en: In the late 1930s and early 1940s, the artist Jackson Pollock was living and working in New York City.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代末和40年代初，艺术家杰克逊·波洛克在纽约市生活和工作。

sentences.en: What was his state of mind, especially after his father died in 1933?
sentences.zh: 他的精神状态如何，特别是1933年他父亲去世后？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't good.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不太好。

sentences.en: You know, Jackson Pollock moved from California to New York to be with his brothers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，杰克逊·波洛克从加利福尼亚搬到纽约是为了和他的兄弟们在一起。

sentences.en: When his father died, he had, you know, extreme depression and alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 他父亲去世时，你知道，他有极度抑郁和酗酒问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, he was taking sculpting classes, but he was just not very happy, very mentally disturbed, having a lot of problems with depression and alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他当时在上雕塑课，但就是很不快乐，精神非常困扰，有严重的抑郁和酗酒问题。

sentences.en: I understand that Jackson Pollock's volatility, combined with this heavy drinking, led to some very public and private meltdowns?
sentences.zh: 据我了解，杰克逊·波洛克反复无常的情绪加上大量饮酒，导致了一些公开和私下的崩溃？

sentences.en: Yes, at an art gallery, he yelled that he was a much better artist than anyone that had their art being displayed in the art gallery.
sentences.zh: 是的，在一家艺术画廊里，他大喊大叫，说自己比画廊里展出作品的任何艺术家都要优秀得多。

sentences.en: And subsequently, he lost the ability to be in that art gallery.
sentences.zh: 随后，他失去了在那家艺术画廊呆下去的资格。

sentences.en: He got into an argument one time and was so angry that he turned over a whole table that had all of the food on the table and, like,
sentences.zh: 有一次他跟人争吵，愤怒到掀翻了一整张摆满食物的桌子，就像，

sentences.en: 12 roast beef dinners were just flying all over the place.
sentences.zh: 12份烤牛肉晚餐到处飞溅。

sentences.en: It was a huge mess, essentially ending the dinner party right then and there.
sentences.zh: 这真是一团糟，晚宴就这样戛然而止。

sentences.en: So, at one point, he gets romantically involved with a painter, Lee Krasner, who wants to get him away from New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时候，他与女画家李·克拉斯纳有了浪漫关系，她想把他带离纽约市。

sentences.en: What was her plan, Mark?
sentences.zh: 马克，她的计划是什么？

sentences.en: I think she wanted to get him out of the New York environment where, you know, there were so many bars that he frequented to remove him from that environment,
sentences.zh: 我想她是想把他带出纽约的环境，在那里，你知道，有很多他常去的酒吧，从而将他从那种环境中移除，

sentences.en: maybe also removing him from some of the people that he was hanging around at the time,
sentences.zh: 也许也让他远离当时和他混在一起的一些人，

sentences.en: and to maybe sort of take him to a more natural, a quieter environment out in Long Island, that the fresh air might be good for him.
sentences.zh: 也许把他带到一个长岛更自然、更安静的环境中，新鲜空气可能对他的健康有益。

sentences.en: Do you know what this place was like that they ended up moving out to?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们最后搬去的地方是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: I think it was, like, in Springs, Long Island, which is in East Hampton.
sentences.zh: 我想它就像是在长岛斯普林斯，也就是东汉普顿。

sentences.en: And it was a pretty modest home, but it had, like, a barn and maybe an acre of land.
sentences.zh: 那是一栋相当简朴的房子，但有一个谷仓，可能还有一英亩的土地。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of sort of beautiful nature to look at, and it did seem to inspire some changes in Jackson.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多美丽的自然风光可供欣赏，这似乎确实激发了杰克逊的一些改变。

sentences.en: What changes?
sentences.zh: 什么改变？

sentences.en: He was no longer as volatile.
sentences.zh: 他不再那么反复无常了。

sentences.en: He was no longer as depressed.
sentences.zh: 他不再那么沮丧了。

sentences.en: And it seemed like being in that environment was also quite inspirational for his artwork.
sentences.zh: 而且身处那样的环境似乎也为他的艺术创作带来了很多灵感。

sentences.en: He would purchase these large yachting canvases, and he would spread them out in the barn in the backyard of his home.
sentences.zh: 他会购买这些大型游艇帆布，并将它们铺在他家后院的谷仓里。

sentences.en: And he started to do his famous, you know, paint splattering, where he would spill the paint and do different things with brushstrokes that were more organic
sentences.zh: 他开始创作他著名的，你知道的，泼墨画，他会把颜料泼洒出去，并用更有机的笔触进行各种操作，

sentences.en: and matched the organic properties of nature.
sentences.zh: 并且符合大自然的有机属性。

sentences.en: And I think people think that being out in nature inspired this new art form for him.
sentences.zh: 我想人们认为置身大自然激发了他这种新的艺术形式。

sentences.en: Now, I understand that he continued to have trouble the rest of his life, so it's not like being out in nature was a panacea.
sentences.zh: 现在，据我了解，他余生中一直有麻烦，所以置身大自然并非万灵药。

sentences.en: It's not like he basically, you know, turned over a completely new leaf.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他基本上，你知道的，彻底翻开了新的一页。

sentences.en: But it did sound as if he got his life together, partly as a result by being out in nature.
sentences.zh: 但听起来他确实理顺了自己的生活，部分原因就是置身大自然。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, we would never argue that depression or alcoholism are easy problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们绝不会争辩说抑郁或酗酒是容易解决的问题。

sentences.en: But it does seem to be the case that people's interactions with nature can be very beneficial for people who are suffering from depression and anxiety or ADHD,
sentences.zh: 但对于遭受抑郁、焦虑或多动症困扰的人来说，人们与大自然的互动似乎确实非常有益，

sentences.en: even things like PTSD.
sentences.zh: 甚至像创伤后应激障碍这样的问题。

sentences.en: So while, yes, I wouldn't say that being in nature can solve all these problems,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我不会说置身大自然能解决所有这些问题，

sentences.en: it does seem to be the case that being and interacting with nature can help with many of these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但身处并与大自然互动似乎确实对其中的许多问题有所帮助。

sentences.en: In more recent years, Mark, the Naval Health Research Center in San Diego, California, has run a program to treat members of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 近年来，马克，加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥的海军健康研究中心开展了一个项目，旨在治疗美国军人。

sentences.en: military.
sentences.zh: 军人。

sentences.en: What kinds of problems are these veterans struggling with?
sentences.zh: 这些老兵正在与什么样的问题作斗争？

sentences.en: Often they have problems that involve maybe developing depression or post-traumatic stress disorder, PTSD.
sentences.zh: 他们经常遇到涉及可能发展为抑郁症或创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的问题。

sentences.en: Some of them have traumatic brain injury or TBI.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人有创伤性脑损伤或TBI。

sentences.en: There's a lot of, you know, physical and mental health conditions that, unfortunately, a lot of these service members develop from their time in the military.
sentences.zh: 有很多，你知道的，身体和心理健康状况，不幸的是，许多这些军人在军旅生涯中患上了这些疾病。

sentences.en: So the psychologists who work with this population take an unusual approach to treatment.
sentences.zh: 因此，与这个群体合作的心理学家采取了一种不同寻常的治疗方法。

sentences.en: What do they do?
sentences.zh: 他们做了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they actually had about 20 or so of these military veterans engage in a six-week surf therapy therapeutic session where for three or four hours in a group setting in a Southern California beach,
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上让大约20名左右的退伍军人参加了一个为期六周的冲浪治疗课程，在南加州海滩的一个小组环境中，时间为三到四个小时，

sentences.en: they taught these veterans how to surf, thinking that this kind of program could actually be beneficial to them from a mental and physical health perspective.
sentences.zh: 他们教这些老兵如何冲浪，认为这种项目实际上可以从身心健康的角度对他们大有裨益。

sentences.en: I'm curious, why surfing?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，为什么是冲浪？

sentences.en: Well, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I think in part because they had some feeling that being in nature might be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是因为他们觉得置身大自然可能会有益。

sentences.en: So being out in the ocean, seeing the ocean waves, being on the beach, having the sights, smells, and even the textures of the ocean could be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 因此，身处海洋中，看海浪，在海滩上，拥有海洋的视觉、气味甚至触觉都可能是有益的。

sentences.en: It was also somewhat of a social activity because they were taking these veterans out in groups of about 20 people.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种社交活动，因为他们把这些老兵以大约20人为一组带出去。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you're trying to catch a wave, sometimes there's a lot of sitting on your board waiting to catch a wave.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你试图赶海浪时，有时会有很多时间坐在冲浪板上等待海浪。

sentences.en: And, of course, too, there's also an exercise component to it.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有运动的成分。

sentences.en: Surfing is challenging.
sentences.zh: 冲浪具有挑战性。

sentences.en: It's a hard physical exercise, and I think they probably also thought that that would be helpful as well.
sentences.zh: 这是一项艰苦的体育锻炼，我想他们可能也认为这会有所帮助。

sentences.en: So the psychologists at the Naval Health Research Center wrote up the results of the surf therapy program in a journal article published in 2019.
sentences.zh: 因此，海军健康研究中心的心理学家在2019年发表的一篇期刊文章中撰文报道了冲浪治疗项目的结果。

sentences.en: What did they report?
sentences.zh: 他们报告了什么？

sentences.en: They found that PTSD symptoms and depression symptoms went down when these surfers were involved in the program,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当这些冲浪者参与该项目时，他们的创伤后应激障碍症状和抑郁症状有所下降，

sentences.en: and they also had sort of improved moods, so more positive mood, less negative mood,
sentences.zh: 他们的情绪也有所改善，也就是说更积极的情绪，更少消极的情绪，

sentences.en: and that the severity of their depression and anxiety symptoms tended to decrease amongst these surf therapy participants.
sentences.zh: 并且这些冲浪治疗参与者的抑郁和焦虑症状的严重程度往往有所下降。

sentences.en: I understand that you yourself sought solace and comfort in nature when you were a stressed-out graduate student at the University of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，当你作为密歇根大学一名压力山大的研究生时，你自己也曾在自然中寻求慰藉和安慰。

sentences.en: Where would you go when you were feeling at your wit's end, Mark?
sentences.zh: 马克，当你感到黔驴技穷时，你会去哪里？

sentences.en: Yeah, the two main places that I would go to were Barton Park.
sentences.zh: 是的，我去的两个主要地方是巴顿公园。

sentences.en: That was kind of right on the Huron River in Ann Arbor, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 那里就在密歇根州安阿伯市的休伦河畔。

sentences.en: And I would also often go to the Ann Arbor Botanical Gardens, which was a little bit farther away from campus,
sentences.zh: 我还会经常去安阿伯植物园，那里离校园稍微远一点，

sentences.en: a little bit, you know, farther away from where I lived, but a very beautiful botanical garden
sentences.zh: 离我住的地方稍微远一点，但那是一个非常美丽的植物园，

sentences.en: that had a lot of nature trails that you could walk on.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多你可以步行的小自然小径。

sentences.en: I understand there was one particular tree at Barton Park that caught your eye?
sentences.zh: 据我了解，巴顿公园里有一棵特别的树吸引了你的目光？

sentences.en: Yeah, there was this, you know, gigantic oak tree kind of in the middle of the trail on Barton Park.
sentences.zh: 是的，巴顿公园的小径中央有一棵巨大的橡树。

sentences.en: It was almost kind of off by itself, this kind of singular oak tree that had a really, really giant trunk,
sentences.zh: 它几乎孤零零地立在那里，是一棵拥有非常非常巨大树干的独特的橡树，

sentences.en: and it always kind of caught my eye.
sentences.zh: 它总是吸引我的目光。

sentences.en: You definitely could hear the wind kind of rustling through its leaves.
sentences.zh: 你绝对能听到风在其树叶中沙沙作响。

sentences.en: And, you know, sometimes I even felt like I would kind of, you know, talk to this majestic tree
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有时我甚至觉得自己会，你知道的，对这棵雄伟的树说话，

sentences.en: that I kind of would anthropomorphize this tree that it could listen to me
sentences.zh: 我把这棵树拟人化了，觉得它能听我倾听，

sentences.en: and maybe kind of help me sort out some of my probleMs.
sentences.zh: 也许能帮我理清我的一些问题。

sentences.en: I understand that toward the end of your time in graduate school, your longtime girlfriend broke up with you.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，在研究生生涯接近尾声时，你交往很久的女友和你分手了。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened and the effect this had on you, Mark.
sentences.zh: 马克，告诉我发生了什么以及这对你有什么影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was very difficult, and I'm sure a lot of people have experienced difficult breakups,
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常困难，我确信很多人都经历过艰难的分手，

sentences.en: but it was, you know, one of my more serious relationships.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是我较为严肃的恋爱关系之一。

sentences.en: And maybe I thought this would be a very long-term, you know, relationship,
sentences.zh: 也许我认为这是一段非常长期的，你知道的关系，

sentences.en: possibly somebody that I would get married to.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是我会结婚的人。

sentences.en: So that was a big blow to me, and I was seeing friends of mine that were getting married or buying houses
sentences.zh: 所以这对我是个沉重的打击，我看到我的朋友们结婚或买房，

sentences.en: or, you know, having kids.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，有了孩子。

sentences.en: They all seemed to be kind of passing me.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎都超越了我。

sentences.en: So it was a very kind of hard time.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一段非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: A lot of things compounded where it did seem like, you know, a lot of my friends were passing me by,
sentences.zh: 很多事情交织在一起，看起来确实是，你知道，我的很多朋友都超越了我，

sentences.en: and I was kind of stuck still maybe being a kid, not really having grown up yet.
sentences.zh: 而我还卡在原地，可能还是个孩子，还没有真正长大。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering how you dealt with this breakup and whether nature played any role in you finding yourself.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道你是如何处理这场分手的，大自然在帮你找回自我方面是否发挥了任何作用。

sentences.en: Well, it certainly did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然有。

sentences.en: I immediately went to Barton Park and looked for that big oak tree to share my sorrow
sentences.zh: 我立刻去了巴顿公园，寻找那棵大橡树来倾诉我的悲伤，

sentences.en: and try to see if that oak tree could heal me a bit.
sentences.zh: 并试图看看那棵橡树是否能治愈我一点。

sentences.en: Standing beneath the majestic branches and the gently rustling leaves,
sentences.zh: 站在雄伟的树枝和沙沙作响的树叶下，

sentences.en: Mark confided his sorrows to the tree.
sentences.zh: 马克向这棵树倾诉了他的悲伤。

sentences.en: I basically said, you know, it's over with me and Heather.
sentences.zh: 我基本上说，你知道，我和希瑟结束了。

sentences.en: Now I've got to move out and find a new place to live.
sentences.zh: 现在我得搬出去找个新地方住了。

sentences.en: I'm single.
sentences.zh: 我是单身。

sentences.en: I don't have much money, and I'm nearly 30.
sentences.zh: 我没有多少钱，而且我快30岁了。

sentences.en: My friends are buying houses.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们都在买房子。

sentences.en: They're getting married.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚了。

sentences.en: They're having kids themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己也有孩子了。

sentences.en: You know, I just felt like a loser and, you know, kind of thinking, what am I doing wrong?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是觉得自己像个失败者，你知道的，心里想，我到底在做什么错事？

sentences.en: What was the effect of saying this to the tree?
sentences.zh: 对这棵树说这些话有什么效果？

sentences.en: Well, initially it didn't help too much, but I think it felt good to get it out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初并没有太大帮助，但我认为把话说出来感觉很好。

sentences.en: When you're in front of majestic nature, and, you know, to me this tree was fairly awe-inspiring,
sentences.zh: 当你站在雄伟的大自然面前时，你知道，对我来说这棵树相当令人敬畏，

sentences.en: it does sort of make your problems feel a little bit smaller, that we're part of something larger,
sentences.zh: 它确实会让你觉得你的问题变小了一点，我们是更宏大事物的一部分，

sentences.en: and the vastness of nature can make us feel small, but I think in a good way,
sentences.zh: 大自然的浩瀚可以让我们感到自己很渺小，但我认为这是以一种好的方式，

sentences.en: where we realize, you know, we're part of something bigger, and, you know, while I certainly was not
sentences.zh: 我们意识到，你知道，我们是更大事物的一部分，而且，你知道，虽然我当时确实感觉不好，

sentences.en: feeling good at the time, that it would pass, and I would get back to being myself again.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都会过去，我会重新做回自己。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes when I'm out in the woods and I see one of these trees that's been around for
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时当我在树林里看到这样一棵已经存在了

sentences.en: 50, 60, 70, 80 years, I can't help but think about all the things that this tree has seen,
sentences.zh: 50、60、70、80年的树时，我不禁会想起这棵树所见过的一切事物，

sentences.en: and all of the historical events that it's witnessed.
sentences.zh: 以及它所见证过的所有历史事件。

sentences.en: I mean, there are trees around that are 200 years old, and you realize that they have seen
sentences.zh: 我是说，周围有些树已经有两百年历史了，你意识到它们见证了

sentences.en: and been around so much, and in some ways, as you talk to the tree about your breakup,
sentences.zh: 并且经历了那么多，某种程度上，当你向树诉说你的分手经历时，

sentences.en: you're putting things in perspective, not just spatially, but also in a question of time.
sentences.zh: 你是在用一种宏观的视角看待事物，不仅是空间上的，也是时间上的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a really, really good point,
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这是一个非常非常好的观点，

sentences.en: and also, too, that you're describing these trees that can be so old.
sentences.zh: 而且，你所描述的这些树木可以如此长寿，

sentences.en: They do kind of have sort of the wisdom of a grandparent, it seems like, you know,
sentences.zh: 它们似乎确实带有一种祖父母般的智慧，你知道的，

sentences.en: they have deep roots, they have a long history.
sentences.zh: 它们根基深厚，有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: It seems like there is some wisdom that's contained in these trees.
sentences.zh: 这些树木中似乎蕴含着某种智慧。

sentences.en: An artist finds relief from his roiling emotions and destructive drinking
sentences.zh: 一位艺术家在长岛乡村的一条小溪旁

sentences.en: alongside a creek in rural Long Island.
sentences.zh: 找到了缓解其汹涌情绪和破坏性饮酒的方法。

sentences.en: Military veterans recover from trauma as they surf the waves of the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 退伍军人在太平洋的浪潮中从创伤中恢复。

sentences.en: And a scientist finds that in the midst of stress and heartbreak,
sentences.zh: 而一位科学家发现，在压力和心碎之中，

sentences.en: a tree can provide the soothing support he needs.
sentences.zh: 一棵树能够提供他所需的舒缓支持。

sentences.en: What is it about being outdoors that soothes and heals us,
sentences.zh: 置身户外究竟有什么魔力，能安抚和治愈我们，

sentences.en: allowing us to become focused and productive?
sentences.zh: 让我们变得专注而高效？

sentences.en: When we come back, the science behind the power of nature to restore our minds.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探究大自然恢复我们心智力量背后的科学。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Have you had experiences in nature that have proved restorative or cleansing?
sentences.zh: 你有没有过在大自然中获得恢复或涤荡的经历？

sentences.en: If you have a story about a time in your life when the great outdoors proved helpful to your inner state of mind,
sentences.zh: 如果你的人生中曾有过某个时刻，大自然对你的内心状态大有裨益，并想分享这个故事，

sentences.en: please find a quiet room and record a short voice memo.
sentences.zh: 请找一个安静的房间，录制一段简短的语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Email it to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 将其发送至我们的邮箱：ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty.
sentences.zh: 两三分钟就足够了。

sentences.en: Please use the subject line, nature.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题请填写：nature。

sentences.en: Mark Berman is a psychologist at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 马克·伯曼是芝加哥大学的一名心理学家。

sentences.en: For many years now, he's been interested in the science of why nature seems to help our minds.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直对大自然似乎能帮助我们心智的科学原理很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Mark, one of the leading lights in your field is a man named Roger Ulrich.
sentences.zh: 马克，你们领域的一位泰斗叫罗杰·乌尔里希。

sentences.en: When he was a teenager, he was often sick.
sentences.zh: 他青少年时期经常生病。

sentences.en: How did he turn to nature to help him?
sentences.zh: 他是如何通过大自然来帮助自己的？

sentences.en: Yeah, he actually told me that when he was a kid or a teenager,
sentences.zh: 是的，他实际上告诉我，当他还是个孩子或青少年时，

sentences.en: he suffered from staph infections and some kidney disease.
sentences.zh: 他饱受葡萄球菌感染和某种肾病的折磨。

sentences.en: And he would spend a lot of times, you know, sitting in clinics or hospitals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他经常花很多时间坐在诊所或医院里。

sentences.en: But he much more enjoyed recuperating at home where he would kind of lie down and out of the window.
sentences.zh: 但他更喜欢在家休养，那时他会躺着望向窗外。

sentences.en: There was a giant pine tree outside his window that he would look at quite often when he was recovering from these illnesses.
sentences.zh: 他窗外有一棵巨大的松树，他在这些疾病康复期间经常看着它。

sentences.en: So he went on to become a researcher.
sentences.zh: 后来他成为了一名研究人员。

sentences.en: And in the early 1980s, he conducted a remarkable study at a hospital in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代初，他在费城的一家医院进行了一项 remarquable（注：此处按自然流畅翻译）的研究。

sentences.en: What did he study and what did he find?
sentences.zh: 他研究了什么？又发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really incredible study.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一项非常不可思议的研究。

sentences.en: And I would say, you know, one of the most seminal works in kind of environmental psychology.
sentences.zh: 我想说，你知道的，这是环境心理学领域最具开创性的著作之一。

sentences.en: And what Roger did was he studied patient recovery from gallbladder surgery on a single corridor in a hospital in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 罗杰做的是，他在费城一家医院的同一走廊里研究了胆囊手术患者的康复情况。

sentences.en: And what Roger was interested in looking at were the views out of the windows of these hospital rooMs.
sentences.zh: 罗杰感兴趣的是观察这些医院病房窗外的景色。

sentences.en: So some of the hospital rooms had some modest views of nature out of the window, like some trees or some shrubs or some grass.
sentences.zh: 因此，一些病房的窗外有一些适度的自然景观，比如一些树木、灌木或草地。

sentences.en: But other rooms on this hospital corridor had views of like a brick wall of the other side of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 但这条医院走廊里的其他病房，窗外看到的是医院另一侧的砖墙之类的景色。

sentences.en: And Roger was interested in seeing, does the room that people are in and the view that they have out the window have any impact on recovery from gallbladder surgery?
sentences.zh: 罗杰有兴趣了解，病人所在的房间以及他们窗外的景色是否对胆囊手术的恢复有任何影响？

sentences.en: And incredibly,
sentences.zh: 难以置信的是，

sentences.en: he found that patients that had the views of modest nature out of their window recovered about a day earlier from gallbladder surgery compared to the patients who had rooms of a brick wall.
sentences.zh: 他发现，窗外能看到适度自然景观的患者比面对砖墙病房的患者，胆囊手术的恢复时间大约早了一天。

sentences.en: In addition, the patients that had the rooms with the nature view, they used less pain medication than the patients that had the views of the brick wall.
sentences.zh: 此外，拥有自然景观病房的患者比面对砖墙景观的患者使用的止痛药更少。

sentences.en: And, you know, people might be thinking, well, maybe patients who were healthier or younger or wealthier, maybe they got the views of nature and the other patients didn't.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，人们可能会想，也许那些更健康、更年轻或更富有的患者分配到了自然景观，而其他患者没有。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: These patients were basically randomly assigned to these different hospital rooMs.
sentences.zh: 这些患者基本上是随机分配到这些不同的病房的。

sentences.en: They were just, whatever room was available, that's the room that they got, which is kind of like doing an experiment.
sentences.zh: 他们只是根据哪个房间可用，就住进哪个房间，这有点像在做实验。

sentences.en: And it's just amazing that being randomly assigned to the room that had the modest nature view could speed recovery and also cause people to use less pain medication.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，仅仅是随机分配到拥有适度自然景观的房间，就能加速康复，并减少人们对止痛药的使用。

sentences.en: Roger was really interested also in stress and stress responses.
sentences.zh: 罗杰对压力和压力反应也非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: So he believed that interactions with nature could remediate stress responses.
sentences.zh: 因此，他认为与大自然的互动可以改善压力反应。

sentences.en: And he thought that was the mechanism behind why interacting with nature was having different beneficial effects.
sentences.zh: 他认为这就是为什么与大自然互动会产生各种有益效果的内在机制。

sentences.en: Over time, many other theories have been advanced about why nature could have positive effects on our minds.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，关于为什么大自然会对我们的心智产生积极影响，人们提出了许多其他理论。

sentences.en: One came from the evolutionary biologist E.O.
sentences.zh: 其中一个来自进化生物学家E.O.

sentences.en: Wilson.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊。

sentences.en: He called it the biophilia hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 他称之为生物ophilia（亲生命）假说。

sentences.en: So the biophilia hypothesis, in a nutshell, is this idea that humans have an inherent love of nature and the natural world and other living organisMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，亲生命假说简而言之就是这样一种观点：人类对大自然、自然界以及其他生命体有着一种与生俱来的热爱。

sentences.en: You know, and these tend to be places that we would say would be very good habitats for humans to live in.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些往往是我们认为非常适合人类居住的栖息地。

sentences.en: And there was actually a researcher, Jay Appleton, who proposed this other theory called prospect refuge theory, that environments that had high prospect, meaning, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，曾有一位研究员杰伊·阿普尔顿提出了另一种名为“展望-庇护”理论的假说，即那些具有高度展望性的环境，意思是，你知道的，

sentences.en: places where you could draw food and water, but also that had high refuge, places where you could kind of hide and be safe, would be the most kind of preferred environments.
sentences.zh: 在这里你可以获取食物和水源，同时也具有高度庇护性的地方，即你可以隐藏并感到安全的地方，将是最受青睐的环境。

sentences.en: And that also kind of matches this idea of humans kind of liking natural environments that have a lot of plants and trees, but also water.
sentences.zh: 这也符合人类喜欢拥有大量植物、树木以及水源的自然环境这一理念。

sentences.en: As you began to conduct your own research in this field, Mark, you were working with a mentor named Stephen Kaplan.
sentences.zh: 马克，当你开始在这个领域进行自己的研究时，你曾与一位名叫斯蒂芬·卡普兰的导师合作。

sentences.en: Steve believed that the benefits of exposure to nature had much to do with attention.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂夫认为，接触大自然所带来的好处很大程度上与注意力有关。

sentences.en: And he would often talk about how humans have two distinct types of attention.
sentences.zh: 他经常谈到人类拥有两种截然不同的注意力。

sentences.en: What are these two forms of attention?
sentences.zh: 这两种形式的注意力是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Steve coined or developed this hypothesis called the attention restoration theory.
sentences.zh: 所以斯蒂夫提出了或发展了这个名为“注意力恢复理论”的假说。

sentences.en: And he did this in partnership with his wife, Rachel Kaplan.
sentences.zh: 他是与妻子瑞秋·卡普兰合作完成这一点的。

sentences.en: And one of the main tenets of attention restoration theory is that humans have two main kinds of attention.
sentences.zh: 注意力恢复理论的主要原则之一是人类拥有两种主要的注意力。

sentences.en: And one kind of attention is called directed attention.
sentences.zh: 其中一种注意力被称为定向注意力。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of attention where you as the individual person are deciding what to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 这就是作为个体的你决定将注意力放在哪里的那种注意力。

sentences.en: So presumably, anybody listening to this show is deciding to pay attention to what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 据推测，收听这个节目的任何人都在决定关注我们正在谈论的内容。

sentences.en: And this directed attention is the kind of attention that we use a lot in schools and at work.
sentences.zh: 这种定向注意力是我们经常在学校和工作中用到的一种注意力。

sentences.en: It's thought to be fatigable or depletable, that you can only sort of direct your attention for so long before you become mentally fatigued and you can't really focus anymore.
sentences.zh: 人们认为它是容易疲劳或消耗的，你只能将注意力集中一段时间，然后就会精神疲劳，无法真正集中精力了。

sentences.en: And we've all had that sensation kind of at the end of a long work day where you might be just staring at the computer screen and nothing's really happening.
sentences.zh: 我们在漫长工作日的结束时都有过这种感觉，你可能只是盯着电脑屏幕，却什么也做不进去。

sentences.en: And you just can't focus or concentrate to get your work done.
sentences.zh: 你就是无法集中精力或专心完成工作。

sentences.en: We would call that a directed attention fatigue state.
sentences.zh: 我们会称之为定向注意力疲劳状态。

sentences.en: And that's a good time to take a break.
sentences.zh: 而那是一个休息的好时机。

sentences.en: So Steve argued that there was a second form of attention as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，斯蒂夫认为还有第二种形式的注意力。

sentences.en: What is the second form?
sentences.zh: 第二种形式是什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And the second form of attention, Steve called involuntary attention.
sentences.zh: 第二种注意力，斯蒂夫称之为非自主注意力。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of attention that's automatically captured by interesting stimulation in the environment.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种被环境中有趣刺激自动捕获的注意力。

sentences.en: So bright lights, loud noises, they automatically capture our attention and we don't really have any control over it.
sentences.zh: 所以耀眼的灯光、巨大的噪音，它们会自动吸引我们的注意力，而我们对此其实没有任何控制权。

sentences.en: And it's thought that involuntary attention is less susceptible to fatigue or depletion.
sentences.zh: 人们认为非自主注意力较不易产生疲劳或消耗。

sentences.en: And you don't often hear people say, oh, I can't look at that beautiful waterfall anymore.
sentences.zh: 你不会经常听到有人说：“哦，我再也无法看那个美丽的瀑布了。”

sentences.en: It's just too beautiful.
sentences.zh: “它实在太美了。”

sentences.en: It's too tiring to look at.
sentences.zh: “看着太累了。”

sentences.en: I have to stop looking at it.
sentences.zh: “我必须停止看它。”

sentences.en: So the idea behind attention restoration theory is that if you can find environments that don't place a lot of demands on directed attention while simultaneously having interesting stimulation that activates the involuntary attention,
sentences.zh: 因此，注意力恢复理论背后的理念是，如果你能找到那些对定向注意力没有太高要求，同时又具有能够激活非自主注意力的有趣刺激的环境，

sentences.en: you could restore or replenish this precious directed attention resource.
sentences.zh: 你就可以恢复或补充这种宝贵的定向注意力资源。

sentences.en: And we think that a lot of natural environments sort of meet these criteria.
sentences.zh: 我们认为许多自然环境在某种程度上符合这些标准。

sentences.en: Not all forms of involuntary attention are restorative.
sentences.zh: 并非所有形式的非自主注意力都具有恢复功能。

sentences.en: Compare the experience of watching ocean waves at a beach, for example, to the experience of walking through Times Square in New York City.
sentences.zh: 例如，将海滩上观赏海浪的体验与穿过纽约市时代广场的体验进行比较。

sentences.en: When you're looking at those waves at the ocean, it captures your involuntary attention, but it doesn't really capture all of your attentional resources.
sentences.zh: 当你看着大海中的那些波浪时，它会吸引你的非自主注意力，但它其实并没有占用你全部的注意力资源。

sentences.en: You can kind of mind wander and think about other things while you're looking at those waves.
sentences.zh: 看着那些海浪时，你可以漫无目的地神游并思考其他事情。

sentences.en: When you're walking through Times Square, it's also very interesting.
sentences.zh: 当你走过时代广场时，它也非常有趣。

sentences.en: There's a lot of really interesting stimulation in Times Square that automatically captures involuntary attention, but it sort of captures all of your attentional resources.
sentences.zh: 时代广场有大量非常有趣的刺激，会自动捕获非自主注意力，但它几乎占用了你所有的注意力资源。

sentences.en: You can't really mind wander or think about other things when you're in Times Square.
sentences.zh: 身处时代广场时，你无法真正神游或思考其他事情。

sentences.en: And Steve and Rachel thought that that kind of stimulation is not really going to be able to rest our directed attention abilities, that it might actually fatigue us even further.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂夫和瑞秋认为，这种刺激并不能真正休息我们的定向注意力能力，它实际上可能会让我们更加疲惫。

sentences.en: This is a crucial point, and I want to take a second to underline it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个至关重要的点，我想花点时间强调一下。

sentences.en: Watching a waterfall or the waves or the clouds drifting across the sky allows our minds to relax, to wander.
sentences.zh: 观看瀑布、海浪或天空中漂浮的云朵能让我们的心灵放松、神游。

sentences.en: These softly fascinating scenes are very different than the harsh demands of being in a hyper-stimulating environment like Times Square.
sentences.zh: 这些柔和迷人的景色与身处时代广场这种高度刺激环境中的严苛要求截然不同。

sentences.en: You cannot let your attention wander.
sentences.zh: 你不能让自己的注意力游离。

sentences.en: You might get bumped into by hordes of tourists or run over by a cab.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被成群的游客撞到，或者被出租车撞倒。

sentences.en: Scientists have also theorized that natural landscapes and soundscapes are just more easily absorbed by our brains.
sentences.zh: 科学家还推测，自然景观和声景更容易被我们的大脑吸收。

sentences.en: There are certain stimulation in the environment that our brains process more fluently, that it's just easier to process certain stimulation.
sentences.zh: 环境中的某些刺激能被我们的大脑更流利地处理，某些刺激就是更容易处理。

sentences.en: And that's also kind of related to soft fascination, that softly fascinating stimulation might also be sort of easier to process.
sentences.zh: 这也与柔和迷人感有关，柔和迷人的刺激可能也更容易处理。

sentences.en: But what does that really mean?
sentences.zh: 但这究竟意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: And so we've started to try to quantify what it means for different stimulation to be processed more fluently or more easily.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开始尝试量化不同的刺激被更流利或更容易地处理意味着什么。

sentences.en: And it seems like that seems to be occurring more for natural images versus urban images.
sentences.zh: 与城市图像相比，自然图像似乎更容易发生这种情况。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: As I'm sitting here talking to you, I'm able to look out at a window and I'm seeing a tree.
sentences.zh: 当我坐在这里跟你说话时，我能够望向窗外，看到一棵树。

sentences.en: And the tree has, you know, probably 5,000 leaves that I can see right now through the window.
sentences.zh: 通过窗户，我此刻能看到这棵树大概有5000片叶子。

sentences.en: But of course, I'm just taking in all of those leaves in one big bite.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我只是一口把所有这些叶子全部收进眼底。

sentences.en: I'm not actually noticing that each of those leaves has a different vein structure and the light is hitting that leaf differently.
sentences.zh: 我其实并没有注意到每一片叶子都有不同的叶脉结构，光线照在叶子上的方式也各不相同。

sentences.en: I'm just taking it in as a tree.
sentences.zh: 我只是把它当作一棵树来接受。

sentences.en: And that's what you're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在这里所谈论的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Versus in the urban environment, you might actually be cataloging all the different objects, you know, that there's a Volkswagen Beetle, a bicycle, you know, Gothic architecture.
sentences.zh: 而在城市环境中，你实际上可能在给所有不同的物体分类，你知道的，有一辆大众甲壳虫、一辆自行车、哥特式建筑。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're just labeling and quantifying all of that information, which is taking up more room.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们只是在给所有这些信息贴标签和量化，这会占用更多的空间。

sentences.en: Whereas what you're saying, when you're looking at that tree, you're compressing that representation to just be a tree and not to, you know,
sentences.zh: 而你所说的，当你看着那棵树时，你将这种表征压缩成仅仅是一棵树，而不是，你知道的，

sentences.en: something that's got 5,000 little extra parts for every single leaf.
sentences.zh: 那种每片叶子都有5000个额外小部件的东西。

sentences.en: One particular aspect of natural settings that might affect us is the prevalence of curved edges.
sentences.zh: 自然环境可能会影响我们的一个特定方面是曲线边缘的普遍存在。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea, Mark.
sentences.zh: 马克，谈谈这个想法吧。

sentences.en: Why would this matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting that natural settings tend to have more curved edges.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的是，自然环境往往有更多的曲线边缘。

sentences.en: You know, if you imagine a tree, a tree's got curvy branches, tend to have curvy leaves, an ocean, the waves are curvy, the coastline is curvy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你想象一棵树，树有弯曲的树枝，通常有弯曲的叶子；大海的波浪是弯曲的，海岸线也是弯曲的。

sentences.en: So nature is filled with curved edges.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然充满了曲线边缘。

sentences.en: And one thing that we found in our research is that people really like images that have more curved edges, even built images.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中发现的一点是，人们真的很喜欢有更多曲线边缘的图像，甚至是建筑图像。

sentences.en: So images of architectural scenes that don't have any nature in them, if the architecture has more curved edges, people tend to like that architecture more.
sentences.zh: 因此，没有任何自然元素的建筑场景图像，如果建筑有更多的曲线边缘，人们往往会更喜欢这种建筑。

sentences.en: Another aspect of natural settings that might affect our minds is the presence of what mathematicians and physicists call fractals.
sentences.zh: 自然环境可能会影响我们心智的另一个方面是数学家和物理学家所说的分形的出现。

sentences.en: What are fractals, Mark, and how do they show up in nature?
sentences.zh: 马克，什么是分形？它们又是如何呈现在自然界中的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so if we imagine a snowflake, the snowflake has a characteristic shape.
sentences.zh: 好的，如果我们想象一片雪花，雪花具有特征性的形状。

sentences.en: If we put that snowflake under a microscope and zoom in, you'll also see some of the same shape.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把这片雪花放在显微镜下放大，你也会看到一些相同的形状。

sentences.en: And if you zoom in some more, you also see the same shape.
sentences.zh: 如果你再放大一些，你还会看到相同的形状。

sentences.en: So that it doesn't really matter what spatial scale you look at the snowflake, it's got this same characteristic shape.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论你以什么空间尺度观察雪花，它都具有这种相同的特征形状。

sentences.en: So we would say then that the snowflake is scale-free.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会说这片雪花是无标度的。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter what spatial scale you look at the snowflake, it's got the same characteristic shape.
sentences.zh: 无论你以什么空间尺度观察雪花，它都具有相同的特征形状。

sentences.en: Or mathematicians would say that that snowflake is more fractal.
sentences.zh: 或者数学家会说这片雪花更具分形特征。

sentences.en: It's got more of a fractal aspect to it.
sentences.zh: 它具有更多的分形属性。

sentences.en: And you can imagine the same thing with a tree.
sentences.zh: 你可以对一棵树想象同样的事情。

sentences.en: A tree has a trunk, which then branches out into other branches, that branches out into smaller branches,
sentences.zh: 一棵树有一个树干，树干延伸出其他树枝，再延伸出更小的树枝，

sentences.en: that might branch out into even smaller branches, that branches out into leaves.
sentences.zh: 这可能会向外延伸出更小的分支，最终延伸到叶片。

sentences.en: And then there's a big vein in the leaf that might branch out into other veins of the leaf.
sentences.zh: 然后叶片中有一条大静脉，它可能会延伸到叶片的其他静脉中。

sentences.en: And so it might not matter as much at what spatial scale you look at the tree.
sentences.zh: 因此，你从哪个空间尺度来观察这棵树可能并不那么重要。

sentences.en: It's kind of got this same branching structure.
sentences.zh: 它基本上具有这种相同的分支结构。

sentences.en: And it turns out nature is filled with this scale-free or fractal stimulation.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，大自然充满了这种无尺度或分形的刺激。

sentences.en: What do you think the role is of these curved edges and fractals in the effects that nature is having on our minds?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些弯曲的边缘和分形在大自然对我们大脑产生的影响中扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: It could be that curved edges, and in particular fractal-ness, might be easier to process.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为弯曲的边缘，特别是分形特性，更容易被处理。

sentences.en: So in particular, if we think about the fractals again, because it's the same shape that's kind of repeating at different scales,
sentences.zh: 因此，特别值得一提的是，如果我们再次思考分形，因为它是以某种方式在不同尺度上重复的相同形状，

sentences.en: you may not have to process or remember every single detail because it's repeated.
sentences.zh: 你可能不需要处理或记住每一个细节，因为它是重复的。

sentences.en: But I also think, too, and, you know, we don't have all the answers to this,
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，而且，你知道，我们对此并没有所有的答案，

sentences.en: it might have to do with an aesthetic preference, that people kind of like symmetry.
sentences.zh: 这可能与审美偏好有关，人们往往喜欢对称。

sentences.en: And this fractal-ness also has some symmetrical properties.
sentences.zh: 这种分形特性也具有一些对称的属性。

sentences.en: People tend not to like sharp edges or straight lines as much.
sentences.zh: 人们往往不太喜欢尖锐的边缘或直线。

sentences.en: You know, you can imagine some buildings, I think, are some buildings that people don't enjoy very much
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以想象一些建筑，我认为，有些人不太喜欢的建筑

sentences.en: tend to be brutalist architecture that's very rectilinear.
sentences.zh: 往往是那种非常方正的粗野主义建筑。

sentences.en: People tend to prefer more gothic architecture that has more intricacy,
sentences.zh: 人们往往更喜欢更精致的哥特式建筑，

sentences.en: or you could imagine a building designed by Gaudi in Barcelona that's very curvy,
sentences.zh: 或者你可以想象由高迪在巴塞罗那设计的非常曲线优美的建筑，

sentences.en: that's mimicking the patterns of nature.
sentences.zh: 它在模仿大自然的图案。

sentences.en: People really seem to enjoy having curved structure in the environment.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎真的很喜欢环境中存在弯曲的结构。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, of course, all of us have been out, you know, on a beautiful day in the woods or by a beach
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所有人都曾在某个美好的日子里外出，你知道，去树林里、海滩边

sentences.en: or in a mountainside, and the weather is great, and, you know, everything looks beautiful.
sentences.zh: 或者山腰上，当时天气很好，而且，你知道，一切看起来都很美。

sentences.en: But you found that even when nature is unpleasant, if you go out in the middle of a snowstorm
sentences.zh: 但你发现，即使在大自然并不令人愉快的时候，如果你走进暴风雪中，

sentences.en: and the roads are slick and the sidewalks are icy, even then, nature can have benefits for us.
sentences.zh: 道路湿滑，人行道结冰，即便如此，大自然也能给我们带来好处。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One of our major studies where we tested directed attention theory involved bringing people into the laboratory
sentences.zh: 我们测试定向注意力理论的主要研究之一，是将人们带到实验室里，

sentences.en: and giving them some objective cognitive tasks to measure their directed attention abilities.
sentences.zh: 给他们一些客观的认知任务来测量他们的定向注意力能力。

sentences.en: And one of these tasks was called the backwards digit span task.
sentences.zh: 其中一项任务被称为倒序数字广度任务。

sentences.en: So participants would hear digits out loud at a pace of about one digit per second.
sentences.zh: 因此，参与者会大声听到数字，速度大约是每秒一个数字。

sentences.en: So four, seven, three.
sentences.zh: 比如，四，七，三。

sentences.en: Four, seven, three.
sentences.zh: 四，七，三。

sentences.en: And the participants would need to repeat those digits back in backwards order.
sentences.zh: 然后参与者需要以倒序重复这些数字。

sentences.en: So three, seven, four.
sentences.zh: 所以是，三，七，四。

sentences.en: And we kept increasing the number of digits up to nine digits.
sentences.zh: 我们不断增加数字的数量，最多增加到九个数字。

sentences.en: Three, one, five, one, six.
sentences.zh: 三，一，五，一，六。

sentences.en: So at around five digits, the task gets very difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以在大约五位数字时，这个任务变得非常困难。

sentences.en: So participants came to the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 因此，参与者来到了实验室。

sentences.en: We gave them this difficult backwards digit span task.
sentences.zh: 我们让他们做了这个困难的倒序数字广度任务。

sentences.en: And then we gave them a map that either had them walk through the Ann Arbor Arboretum, that was our nature walk,
sentences.zh: 然后我们给他们一张地图，让他们穿过安娜堡植物园，这是我们的自然漫步路线，

sentences.en: or we had them walk through busy downtown Ann Arbor, through busy Washtenaw Avenue.
sentences.zh: 或者让他们穿过繁忙的安娜堡市中心，穿过繁华的瓦什特瑙大道。

sentences.en: And then participants returned back to the lab to repeat this backwards digit span task again.
sentences.zh: 接着，参与者返回实验室再次重复这个倒序数字广度任务。

sentences.en: The main effect was we found that participants improved their ability on this backwards digit span task by about 20% after the walk in nature,
sentences.zh: 主要的效果是，我们发现参与者在自然漫步后，他们在这个倒序数字广度任务上的能力提高了大约20%，

sentences.en: but not after the walk in the urban environment.
sentences.zh: 而在城市环境中漫步后则没有这种提高。

sentences.en: So they improved by about a digit and a half just after a 50-minute walk.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅在进行了一次50分钟的散步后，他们的成绩就提高了大约一个半数字。

sentences.en: And many people might be thinking, well, maybe it's just because walking in nature is pleasant and people really like the walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 许多人可能会想，嗯，也许这只是因为在大自然中散步很愉快，人们真的很喜欢在大自然中散步。

sentences.en: And it's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Participants did enjoy the walk in nature for the most part.
sentences.zh: 参与者在很大程度上确实很享受在大自然中的散步。

sentences.en: But we didn't see a strong correlation between how much people like to walk or how much their mood improved on the walk in nature
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有发现，人们有多喜欢散步，或者他们在自然漫步中情绪改善了多少，

sentences.en: being correlated with their improvements on this working memory task, this backwards digit span task.
sentences.zh: 与他们在工作记忆任务（即倒序数字广度任务）上的提高之间存在强烈的相关性。

sentences.en: So it wasn't the case that just the people who loved the nature walk so much were the ones who showed the biggest improvement.
sentences.zh: 因此，并不是只有那些极其热爱自然漫步的人才表现出最大的进步。

sentences.en: And an even stronger demonstration of this is that we had participants walk at different times of the year.
sentences.zh: 而这方面一个更有力的证明是，我们让参与者在一年中的不同时间进行散步。

sentences.en: So some people walked in June when it was about 80 degrees Fahrenheit in Ann Arbor, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些人是在密歇根州安娜堡市气温约华氏80度（约26度）的六月散步的。

sentences.en: And participants said, oh, Mark, I love the walk.
sentences.zh: 参与者说，哦，马克，我很喜欢这次散步。

sentences.en: I can't believe you're paying me to go for a walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信你花钱让我去大自然中散步。

sentences.en: They showed really healthy mood improvements, and they also showed really healthy improvements to directed attention as measured with this backwards digit span task.
sentences.zh: 他们的情绪得到了非常健康的改善，并且通过倒序数字广度任务测量发现，他们的定向注意力也得到了非常健康的改善。

sentences.en: But we also had people walk in January when it was 25 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 但我们也让人们在一月份、气温为华氏25度（约零下4度）时散步。

sentences.en: And participants said, Mark, I was freezing out there.
sentences.zh: 参与者说，马克，我在外面都要冻僵了。

sentences.en: I did not like that walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不喜欢那次在大自然中的散步。

sentences.en: But those participants that walked in January showed the same cognitive improvement as the people that walked in June.
sentences.zh: 但那些在一月份散步的参与者，表现出了与六月份散步的人相同的认知改善。

sentences.en: So sort of the short answer is to get these cognitive benefits, you don't even need to enjoy the nature walk to get the benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以简短的回答是，为了获得这些认知上的好处，你甚至不需要享受自然漫步本身就能获得这些好处。

sentences.en: I mean, that's striking because I think most of us assume that the subjective experience of the walk, the fact that we like the beach, we like the water, we like the sunshine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很惊人，因为我认为我们大多数人都认为散步的主观体验，比如我们喜欢海滩、喜欢水、喜欢阳光。

sentences.en: But I think the study might be arguing that, in fact, the effects that nature is having on our mind are in some ways independent of our enjoyment of it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这项研究可能在说明，事实上，大自然对我们心灵的影响在某些方面独立于我们对它的享受程度。

sentences.en: I think that's right to some extent.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.en: So I definitely don't think all of these effects are driven by preference.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对不认为所有这些影响都是由偏好驱动的。

sentences.en: And you even have people that say, you know, I'm a city lover.
sentences.zh: 你甚至会听到有人说，你知道，我是个城市爱好者。

sentences.en: I don't like being in nature.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢置身于大自然中。

sentences.en: And we don't think that really matters.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这其实没关系。

sentences.en: However, I think if we would have sent those participants in January on the walk in nature without a coat, and they were so uncomfortable,
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为如果我们在一月份让那些参与者不穿外套去大自然散步，以至于他们感到非常不舒服，

sentences.en: I think that would have used a lot of directed attention, and they wouldn't have seen the nature effects.
sentences.zh: 我认为那会消耗大量的定向注意力，他们也就不会看到大自然带来的效果了。

sentences.en: Or if you're walking, you know, in June, and there's so many mosquitoes that you're getting eaten alive, and it's so uncomfortable,
sentences.zh: 或者如果你在六月散步，你知道，有那么多的蚊子叮咬你，让你感到非常不舒服，

sentences.en: I don't think we would see the effects.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们就不会看到这种效果了。

sentences.en: But I think as long as basic safety and comfort needs are met, you don't have to really love the nature interaction to get these cognitive benefits.
sentences.zh: 但我想，只要基本的安全和舒适需求得到满足，你并不非得真正热爱与大自然的互动才能获得这些认知上的好处。

sentences.en: So you can go on a cloudy day, you could go on a rainy day, you can go on a cold day.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在阴天去，可以在下雨天去，可以在寒冷的日子去。

sentences.en: As long as your basic safety and comfort needs are met, we think you can get these benefits.
sentences.zh: 只要你的基本安全和舒适需求得到满足，我们认为你就能获得这些好处。

sentences.en: Being in nature boosts our mood, reduces our stress, and restores our attention.
sentences.zh: 置身于大自然中可以提升我们的情绪，减轻我们的压力，并恢复我们的注意力。

sentences.en: When we come back, how we can intentionally harness the power of nature to make our own minds work better.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将探讨如何有意识地利用大自然的力量，让我们的头脑更好地运转。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔。

sentences.en: Have you had experiences in nature that have proved restorative or cleansing?
sentences.zh: 你是否有过在大自然中获得恢复或净化的经历？

sentences.en: If you have a story about a time in your life where the great outdoors proved helpful to your inner state of mind,
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个关于你生命中的某个时刻，大自然对你的内心状态有所帮助的故事，

sentences.en: please find a quiet room and record a short voice memo.
sentences.zh: 请找一个安静的房间，录制一段简短的语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Email it to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 将其通过电子邮件发送给我们：ideas@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty.
sentences.zh: 两到三分钟就足够了。

sentences.en: Please use the subject line, nature.
sentences.zh: 请使用主题行：nature（自然）。

sentences.en: Mark Berman is a psychologist at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 马克·伯曼是芝加哥大学的一名心理学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of Nature and the Mind, the science of how nature improves cognitive, physical, and social well-being.
sentences.zh: 他是《自然与思维：自然如何改善认知、身体和社交福祉的科学》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Mark, when you've been working hard, you like to take a break by watching sports.
sentences.zh: 马克，当你工作努力时，你喜欢通过观看体育比赛来休息。

sentences.en: You once assumed that this activity was relaxing and refreshing, but you don't believe this anymore?
sentences.zh: 你曾以为这项活动既轻松又提神，但你现在不这么认为了吗？

sentences.en: No, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不，不幸的是。

sentences.en: I think actually watching sports is not really softly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我认为实际上看体育比赛并不是那种柔和迷人的体验。

sentences.en: That's a bit harshly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 那是一种带有一点激烈刺激的吸引。

sentences.en: And even when my team won, sometimes I would feel a bit irritated after watching.
sentences.zh: 甚至当我的球队赢了的时候，有时看完之后我也会觉得有点恼火。

sentences.en: Now, I still love to watch some of my favorite teams, but I don't do that as a reSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，我仍然喜欢观看我的一些最爱球队，但我不会把这当作一种休息。

sentences.en: That's not a reSt.
sentences.zh: 那不是休息。

sentences.en: And I think, unfortunately, there are many other things that we do in the modern world,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，不幸的是，我们在现代生活中做的许多其他事情，

sentences.en: maybe scrolling social media, looking at our news feed, surfing the Internet,
sentences.zh: 也许是刷社交媒体、看新闻动态、上网冲浪，

sentences.en: that might feel like restful activities, but that actually may be depleting activities.
sentences.zh: 这些可能感觉像是让人放松的活动，但实际上可能是消耗精力的活动。

sentences.en: You know, I was talking with some friends just a couple of weeks ago,
sentences.zh: 你知道，就在几周前，我和一些朋友聊天，

sentences.en: and they were telling me about watching a sports match that was very thrilling and had a very, very dramatic conclusion.
sentences.zh: 他们跟我讲述了一场非常惊心动魄、结局极其戏剧性的体育比赛。

sentences.en: And at the end of it, you know, they were describing almost what felt like watching a horror movie
sentences.zh: 在比赛结束时，你知道，他们描述的感觉几乎就像是在看恐怖电影，

sentences.en: because they said, you know, they were literally crouching behind a couch, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为他们说，你知道，他们真的蹲在沙发后面，你知道，

sentences.en: watching the TV afraid of what it was going to show them or covering their faces and looking at the TV
sentences.zh: 看着电视，害怕电视上会显示出什么画面，或者捂着脸透过手指间的缝隙看着电视

sentences.en: through a small gap in their fingers.
sentences.zh: 透过手指间的小缝隙看着电视。

sentences.en: And I think that speaks to the idea that this is not, you know, calmly restorative TV watching.
sentences.zh: 我认为这说明了这样一个观点：这并不是那种，你知道的，让人平静恢复精力的电视观看体验。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I can sympathize with those feelings.
sentences.zh: 我能理解那些感受。

sentences.en: I know what that feels like.
sentences.zh: 我知道那是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And again, I'm not saying that it's bad or that you want to avoid that at all costs.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我并不是说这不好，或者你想不惜一切代价避免这种情况。

sentences.en: Just don't think of that as being a restful activity because it probably isn't.
sentences.zh: 只是不要把它当作一种放松的活动，因为它可能并不是。

sentences.en: So, Mark, we know from lots of lines of psychological research that people misjudge what will make them happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，从大量的心理学研究中我们知道，人们会错误判断什么能让他们快乐。

sentences.en: You say that this is the case when it comes to spending time in nature.
sentences.zh: 你说在花时间亲近自然这方面也是如此。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Yeah, there was an interesting study done by some researchers where they asked participants,
sentences.zh: 是的，研究人员曾做过一项有趣的实验，他们问参与者：

sentences.en: how much do you think you would enjoy going for a walk in nature?
sentences.zh: 你认为自己去大自然中散步会有多享受？

sentences.en: So they sort of had to forecast how much would they like the walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须某种程度上预测他们会有多喜欢在大自然中散步。

sentences.en: And then they had another group of participants walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 然后他们让另一组参与者去大自然中散步。

sentences.en: And then they asked them after the walk, how much did you enjoy the walk in nature?
sentences.zh: 接着在散步结束后，他们问这些人：你有多享受这次大自然散步？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And it turns out people really, really underestimated how much they would enjoy the walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人们大大低估了他们会有多享受在大自然中的散步。

sentences.en: So their forecasts were wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的预测是错误的。

sentences.en: You know, people enjoyed the walk much more than they forecasted it to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们对散步的享受程度远超他们之前的预测。

sentences.en: And that's just about liking the walk.
sentences.zh: 而这还只是关于喜不喜欢散步本身。

sentences.en: I'm guessing that we also are sort of off in our forecast in terms of how helpful or restorative the walk in nature might be.
sentences.zh: 我猜我们在预测自然漫步会有多大帮助或多大恢复作用时，也存在一定的偏差。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if this is connected to the fact that nature is softly fascinating, Mark.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是否与大自然具有柔和迷人的特性有关，马克？

sentences.en: Because, for example, if you asked my friends who watched that very exciting match, was the match exciting?
sentences.zh: 因为，举个例子，如果你问我那些观看那场极其精彩比赛的朋友，比赛精彩吗？

sentences.en: They would have no problem telling you the match was very exciting and was absolutely and absolutely had to be watched.
sentences.zh: 他们会毫不犹豫地告诉你，比赛非常精彩，绝对、绝对非看不可。

sentences.en: On the other hand, when someone goes for a nice walk, precisely because it's softly fascinating, it hasn't captured our attention.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，当一个人去散步时，恰恰因为它是柔和迷人的，它并没有强行吸引我们的注意力。

sentences.en: If you ask someone to forecast how exciting the next walk is going to be, how fun it's going to be, we underestimate it.
sentences.zh: 如果你让某人预测下一次散步会有多精彩、会有多好玩，我们会低估它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: I think that could be part of it, definitely.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对可能是原因之一。

sentences.en: That softly fascinating stimulation might be sort of less enjoyable or less exciting than this more harshly fascinating stimulation.
sentences.zh: 这种柔和迷人的刺激可能比那种更具强烈刺激感的体验乐趣更少或更不令人兴奋。

sentences.en: But that's also part of the phenomenon of why it might work, that it is more restful to go for the walk in nature,
sentences.zh: 但这也是为什么它能起作用的现象的一部分，即去大自然中散步更有放松效果，

sentences.en: even if it's not as enjoyable as doing something else that might be more harshly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 即使它不如做其他可能更具强烈刺激感的事情那么令人享受。

sentences.en: We've been talking a lot about how we're affected by what we see outdoors,
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论我们如何受到户外所见事物的吉凶影响，

sentences.en: but your research has looked at the sounds of nature and how they can make a difference.
sentences.zh: 但你的研究探讨了大自然的声音以及它们如何产生影响。

sentences.en: What do you find, Mark?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么，马克？

sentences.en: So we found that just listening to nature sounds versus urban sounds,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，仅仅聆听自然声音与城市声音相比，

sentences.en: you can get some of these same benefits as walking in nature.
sentences.zh: 你可以获得与在大自然中散步类似的一些好处。

sentences.en: So you can get these improvements on tasks like the backwards digit span task and other cognitive tasks
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以在像倒序数字广度任务以及其他涉及定向注意力的认知任务上获得这些提高，

sentences.en: that involve directed attention, that just listening to about 10 minutes of nature sounds
sentences.zh: 仅仅聆听大约10分钟的自然声音，

sentences.en: can improve performance on these tasks.
sentences.zh: 就能提高在这些任务上的表现。

sentences.en: And I would mention that, you know, we find you get the strongest benefits typically
sentences.zh: 我想指出的是，你知道，我们发现通常当你走到真正的自然中时，你会获得最强的好处，

sentences.en: when going out in real nature, likely because real nature is more softly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为真正的自然更具有柔和迷人的魅力。

sentences.en: It's got the sights, the sounds, maybe even the smells or the textures that might be beneficial to us.
sentences.zh: 它有视觉、声音，甚至可能有对我们有益的气味或触感。

sentences.en: But it's interesting because a lot of us don't have access to real nature.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，我们许多人无法接触到真正的自然。

sentences.en: It's interesting that you can get some of these same improvements with simulated nature,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，通过模拟自然，比如自然声音、自然图片或自然视频，你可以获得一些相同的改善。

sentences.en: like nature sounds or nature pictures or nature videos.
sentences.zh: 像自然声音、自然图片或自然视频。

sentences.en: Do you think doctors should be prescribing nature the way they now prescribe medications, Mark?
sentences.zh: 马克，你认为医生是否应该像现在开处方药一样给患者开具“自然处方”？

sentences.en: Well, in some countries, they already are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某些国家，它们已经开始了。

sentences.en: In the UK, they're prescribing nature walks as a therapy for depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在英国，他们把自然漫步作为抑郁症和焦虑症的处方疗法。

sentences.en: In Canada, they're also prescribing nature walks as a therapy for depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，他们同样将自然漫步作为抑郁症和焦虑症的处方疗法。

sentences.en: I don't think anyone yet would say that interacting with nature would be a replacement therapy
sentences.zh: 我认为目前还没有人会说，亲近自然可以完全替代疗法

sentences.en: for psychotherapy or pharmacological therapies for depression and anxiety,
sentences.zh: 也就是针对抑郁症和焦虑症的心理治疗或药物治疗，

sentences.en: but it certainly could be a supplemental therapy.
sentences.zh: 但它绝对可以作为一种辅助疗法。

sentences.en: And people have also found that interacting with nature can be really helpful for kids with ADHD,
sentences.zh: 人们还发现，亲近自然对患有多动症的孩子非常有帮助，

sentences.en: that brief interactions with nature, like 20 minutes walk in nature,
sentences.zh: 短暂的亲近自然，比如在自然中散步20分钟，

sentences.en: can be as beneficial as a dose of Ritalin.
sentences.zh: 其效果可以媲美一剂利他林。

sentences.en: So I think the research is definitely not there yet in terms of having interactions with nature be a replacement
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为就让亲近自然替代

sentences.en: for any validated forms of therapy for depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 任何针对抑郁症和焦虑症的既定治疗方法而言，相关研究显然还远远不够。

sentences.en: But I do think there's already becoming evidence and doctors are already starting to take this work seriously
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，已经有越来越多的证据表明，并且医生们也开始重视这一研究，

sentences.en: that interactions with nature could be a supplement to existing therapies for like depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 那就是亲近自然可以作为抑郁症等现有疗法的补充。

sentences.en: You know, I remember once taking the elevator to the top of the Washington Monument here in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得有一次在华盛顿特区，我坐电梯登上了华盛顿纪念碑的顶端，

sentences.en: and from that height in my home city looking north,
sentences.zh: 从我所居住的城市的高度向北望去，

sentences.en: I could see that one quadrant of my city was very green and leafy,
sentences.zh: 我看到城市的其中一个区域绿树成荫、郁郁葱葱，

sentences.en: while the other quadrant that I could see was really barren.
sentences.zh: 而我能看到的另一个区域则显得十分荒凉。

sentences.en: Now, the leafy quadrant happened to also be one of the richest parts of Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，绿树成荫的那个区域恰好也是华盛顿特区最富裕的地区之一，

sentences.en: and the barren portion happened to be one of the poorer parts of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 而荒凉的那个部分恰好是华盛顿特区较贫困的地区之一。

sentences.en: Can you talk a moment about how our access to nature is often connected to our socioeconomic status,
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊为什么我们接触自然的机会往往与我们的社会经济地位挂钩吗？

sentences.en: that access to nature is becoming one more way in which social inequality can manifest itself?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，接触自然正逐渐成为社会不平等体现的又一种方式？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there is a correlation between socioeconomics and access to green space,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，社会经济状况与绿地获取之间确实存在某种关联，

sentences.en: and you see that in a lot of cities in the U.S., for example.
sentences.zh: 比如你在美国的好多城市都能看到这种现象。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a lot of different reasons why that might be the case,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，造成这种现象的原因有很多，

sentences.en: and even people have found that, you know, redlined neighborhoods have less green space
sentences.zh: 甚至有人发现，经历过住房歧视划线的社区其绿地空间往往更少，

sentences.en: and less biodiversity than non-redlined neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 生物多样性也比未被划线的社区要少。

sentences.en: So there's deep historical reasons for a lot of this.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切背后有着深厚的历史原因。

sentences.en: The air might be cleaner in wealthier neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 富裕社区的空气可能更清新。

sentences.en: There's likely less pollutants in wealthier neighborhoods than poorer neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 与贫困社区相比，富裕社区的污染物可能更少。

sentences.en: And I think it's sort of an environmental justice issue that this isn't just a nice amenity that wealthy people have.
sentences.zh: 我认为这某种程度上是一个环境正义问题，这不仅仅是富人享有的一项美好便利设施。

sentences.en: This is something fundamental to all humans that we need to have access to these natural spaces,
sentences.zh: 这是全人类的基本需求，我们需要接触这些自然空间，

sentences.en: and if we don't have it, people are going to suffer.
sentences.zh: 如果我们失去了这些，人们就会受到影响。

sentences.en: I understand that you and your wife, Katie, had a difficult decision to make a number of years ago
sentences.zh: 我了解到，你和你的妻子凯蒂在多年前曾面临一个艰难的决定，

sentences.en: when the two of you were living in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 当时你们俩正住在密歇根州。

sentences.en: What was this decision, and how did nature end up playing a role in helping you make this decision, Mark?
sentences.zh: 那是个什么决定？马克，自然最终是如何在帮你做出这个决定时发挥作用的？

sentences.en: I had a job offer in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 我当时在新泽西州得到了一份工作Offer。

sentences.en: It was a professorship.
sentences.zh: 那是一个教授职位。

sentences.en: You know, they're very hard to come by.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这种职位非常难得。

sentences.en: I really wanted to take the job.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想接受这份工作。

sentences.en: But my, you know, wife, Katie, and I, we were pregnant at the time, too.
sentences.zh: 但我的妻子凯蒂和我，我们当时也怀孕了。

sentences.en: And Katie just felt uncomfortable kind of going to a new place where we didn't have family to have our child there.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂觉得很不适应去一个没有家人的新地方生孩子。

sentences.en: So she wanted to go back and be near family in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 所以她想回多伦多，回到家人身边。

sentences.en: And it was a very difficult decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: We were arguing a lot about it.
sentences.zh: 我们为此争论了很久。

sentences.en: It was a very challenging time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段非常具有挑战性的时期。

sentences.en: But we did often talk about this difficult decision in nature.
sentences.zh: 但我们在大自然中确实经常谈论这个艰难的决定。

sentences.en: And I remember walking through the botanical gardens a number of times with Katie,
sentences.zh: 我记得和凯蒂一起多次漫步在植物园里，

sentences.en: you know, talking about all the pros and cons of it.
sentences.zh: 讨论着这其中的种种利弊。

sentences.en: I don't think these were necessarily restorative walks in nature.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些散步未必属于那种能让人恢复精力的自然漫步。

sentences.en: But again, I think being in nature afforded us some directed attention benefits.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，我认为置身于大自然中确实赋予了我们一些定向注意力的益处。

sentences.en: And we did decide that I would give up this job and that we would, I would try to get a postdoc job in Toronto and we would have our first child in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 我们最终决定放弃这份工作，并且尝试在多伦多找一份博士后工作，我们的第一个孩子也将在多伦多出生。

sentences.en: I do remember one time, too, on one of these walks as we were in the botanical gardens, we did see a turtle, like, burying her eggs on the path.
sentences.zh: 我还记得有一次，也是在植物园散步的时候，我们确实看到了一只乌龟在小路上产卵。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, it just kind of made me think, you know, while this is very hard to give up this job and these jobs are very difficult to come by,
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这让我意识到，尽管放弃这份工作很难，而且这类工作也非常难得，

sentences.en: focusing more on the family and what would make the family most comfortable, what would be the best environment for the family was probably the best decision.
sentences.zh: 但把更多精力放在家庭上，考虑什么能让家庭最舒适、什么对家庭而言是最好的环境，或许才是最正确的决定。

sentences.en: Swimming in the ocean, tromping through a field, or wandering through a forest can do wonders for our mental clarity and our attention span.
sentences.zh: 在海里畅游、在田野中穿行，或者在森林中漫步，都能对我们的思维清晰度和注意力持续时间产生奇效。

sentences.en: But most of us spend the bulk of our time inside buildings.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们大多数人绝大部分时间都是在建筑物内部度过的。

sentences.en: When we come back, bringing the benefits of nature indoors.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨如何把大自然的好处带到室内。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: We're talking today to psychologist Mark Berman about nature's effect on the mind.
sentences.zh: 今天我们邀请到心理学家马克·伯曼，来聊聊自然对心灵的影响。

sentences.en: If you have follow-up questions, comments, or stories about your experience of nature that you would be comfortable sharing with the Hidden Brain audience,
sentences.zh: 如果你有后续的问题、评论，或者愿意与《隐藏的大脑》听众分享的亲近自然的经历，

sentences.en: please record a voice memo on your phone and email it to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 请用手机录下一段语音备忘录，并发送电子邮件至 ideas at hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Use the subject line, nature.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题请填写：nature（自然）。

sentences.en: Mark Berman has spent years studying how outdoor spaces influence us.
sentences.zh: 马克·伯曼多年来一直在研究户外空间如何影响我们。

sentences.en: But the fact is that many of us spend most of our time indoors.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们许多人大部分时间都待在室内。

sentences.en: Is it possible to reap the rewards of nature from within a building or even inside a car?
sentences.zh: 我们是否有可能在建筑物内部，甚至在汽车里，也收获大自然的馈赠呢？

sentences.en: Mark, you say that we can intentionally naturize our interior spaces, bring elements of nature indoors.
sentences.zh: 马克，你提到我们可以刻意让室内空间“自然化”，将大自然的元素引入室内。

sentences.en: Before we talk about the how, let's talk about the why.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论具体怎么做之前，先来聊聊为什么这么做。

sentences.en: Why would we do this?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Well, we would do this because we find that even having plants,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们这样做是因为我们发现，即使摆放植物，

sentences.en: even if they're artificial plants in our homes, in our offices, can also lead to some benefits.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是在我们的家 里、办公室里摆放人造植物，也能带来一些好处。

sentences.en: So, and oftentimes it's hard to bring real nature into indoor spaces.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，很难将真正的自然搬进室内空间。

sentences.en: Maybe we don't have enough natural light or it's difficult to water plants on a regular schedule.
sentences.zh: 也许我们没有充足的自然光，或者很难按照固定的时间表给植物浇水。

sentences.en: But it's interesting to note that other researchers have found that bringing nature indoors,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，其他研究人员发现，将自然引入室内，

sentences.en: even if it's fake nature, can have some of these similar benefits.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是假的大自然，也能产生一些类似的好处。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Talk about how you yourself have tried to naturize the spaces in which you live and work.
sentences.zh: 聊聊你是如何尝试让你的生活和工作空间变得更加自然化的吧。

sentences.en: Well, right now I'm in my home office.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我现在正坐在我的家庭办公室里。

sentences.en: I actually have two plants behind me.
sentences.zh: 我身后其实放了两盆植物。

sentences.en: They're actually artificial plants.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是人造植物。

sentences.en: Those aren't real plants.
sentences.zh: 那些不是真植物。

sentences.en: You know, they look fairly real, which I think is good.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们看起来挺逼真的，我觉得这挺好。

sentences.en: But I don't have enough natural light here to actually get real plants in the office.
sentences.zh: 但这里的自然光不够，没法在办公室里养真正的植物。

sentences.en: In other portions of our house, we do actually have real plants.
sentences.zh: 在我们家的其他区域，我们确实养了真正的植物。

sentences.en: So we get some nice light through one of our bay windows.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以通过其中一扇凸窗获得很好的光线。

sentences.en: We have a few different plants there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里摆放了几种不同的植物。

sentences.en: So we try to bring in real nature where we can into our home and where we can't.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在家里条件允许的地方尽量引入真正的自然，而在条件不允许的地方，

sentences.en: We usually utilize some fake nature.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会利用一些人造自然。

sentences.en: It also so happens that my mother-in-law is a little bit of an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，我岳母是一位艺术家。

sentences.en: My sister is a little bit of an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 我妹妹也是一位艺术家。

sentences.en: We've commissioned them to make some nature paintings that we have hanging in our home.
sentences.zh: 我们请她们创作了一些自然主题的画作，挂在家里。

sentences.en: So there are many different kinds of things that we can do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以做很多不同类型的事情。

sentences.en: Some of my kids actually like to sleep with a sound machine.
sentences.zh: 我的几个孩子其实喜欢伴着白噪音机器睡觉。

sentences.en: Often we use nature sounds for them to be playing in the background to help them sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们经常让他们在背景音中播放自然之声来帮助他们入睡。

sentences.en: So I think there's a number of different things that we can do to naturize our spaces.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我们可以做很多不同的事情来让我们的空间自然化。

sentences.en: I understand that one time you were visiting your parents in Detroit and you found that an airport hotel had found a way to naturize its indoor spaces.
sentences.zh: 我听说有一次你去看望底特律的父母时，发现一家机场酒店竟然找到了让室内空间自然化的方法。

sentences.en: Tell me about this experience.
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲这段经历吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 对，挺酷的。

sentences.en: So in Detroit Metro Airport, kind of like off to the side, there's the Westin Hotel.
sentences.zh: 在底特律都会机场，差不多在侧边一点的地方，有一家威斯汀酒店。

sentences.en: And I remember my dad telling me that it's an interesting spot to check out.
sentences.zh: 我记得我父亲告诉我那是一个值得一探的有趣地方。

sentences.en: So I remember taking the escalator down and it was incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得当时坐着自动扶梯下去，眼前的景象令人难以置信。

sentences.en: They had these fake bamboo trees that were out in the lobby of the Westin Hotel and also some water features.
sentences.zh: 威斯汀酒店的大堂里摆放着假竹子，还有一些水景。

sentences.en: And even though it was fake, it almost felt like you were in a different world.
sentences.zh: 尽管是假的，但你几乎会觉得自己身处另一个世界。

sentences.en: And you could feel almost the restorative power of these natural elements, even though a lot of them were fake.
sentences.zh: 你几乎能感受到这些自然元素带来的疗愈力量，尽管其中许多都是假的。

sentences.en: And so every time that I would go to the Detroit Airport, I would often try to go to the Westin Hotel.
sentences.zh: 所以每次去底特律机场，我通常都会尽量去一趟威斯汀酒店。

sentences.en: And there was a little actually TSA security gate there so you could go through security there.
sentences.zh: 那里其实有一个小型TSA安检口，你可以在那儿过安检。

sentences.en: And I would try to do that on a regular basis so I could get exposed to that kind of very interesting natural environment that they had created in the lobby of the Westin Hotel.
sentences.zh: 我会经常这么做，这样就能接触到他们在威斯汀酒店大堂里营造的那种非常有趣的自然环境。

sentences.en: So I've noticed that as I go through airports nowadays, that some of them are making a deliberate attempt to bring the outdoors indoors.
sentences.zh: 我发现现在的我在穿梭于各大机场时，注意到其中一些机场正在刻意尝试将户外景观引入室内。

sentences.en: And sometimes, as you say, this is fake nature.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，有时这些是假大自然。

sentences.en: I've sometimes flown through the airport in Doha in Qatar, and they have reimagined an entire section of the airport to make it look like almost like a wildlife habitat.
sentences.zh: 我有几次飞越卡塔尔多哈机场时，发现他们重新规划了机场的整个区域，使其看起来几乎像是一个野生动物栖息地。

sentences.en: Now, there are some actual trees, but the grass is really just green carpeting.
sentences.zh: 那里确实有一些真树，但草坪其实只是绿色的地毯。

sentences.en: But I find that it's very restorative to stop in this area during stopovers on a long flight.
sentences.zh: 但我发现在长途飞行的中转期间，在这个区域驻足停留非常具有疗愈效果。

sentences.en: Yes, and I've seen it, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也见证过。

sentences.en: Even airports now are starting to have kind of green walls.
sentences.zh: 甚至现在的机场也开始设立所谓的绿化墙。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, it's also kind of near security.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，它也设在安检口附近。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if they have it in there to kind of calm people down as they're waiting in line to go through these security checks.
sentences.zh: 我在想，他们把这个设在那里，是不是为了在人们排队过安检时起到镇静作用。

sentences.en: So I think a lot of these airport designers are having the intuition that incorporating some nature into the airport is going to be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为许多机场设计者都有这样一种直觉：在机场融入一些自然元素会大有裨益。

sentences.en: And people have tried to do similar things in hospitals where, again, oftentimes in hospitals, the environment requires to be sterile, but it has to be sterile.
sentences.zh: 人们也在医院里尝试过类似的做法，虽然医院的环境往往要求保持无菌，但它必须是无菌的。

sentences.en: But people have brought in fake nature into hospitals, and they found that it can reduce pain for people that are getting painful operations.
sentences.zh: 不过人们还是把假大自然引入了医院，他们发现这可以减轻接受痛苦手术的病人的疼痛。

sentences.en: It can make people feel like their stay in the hospital is more enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 这能让人觉得他们在医院的滞留体验更加愉快。

sentences.en: And this is even when they know, the patients know, that the plants are fake.
sentences.zh: 即便是在病人们知道这些植物是假的情况下，也是如此。

sentences.en: And it can also have benefits to the people working in the hospital that it can maybe help to give them these, as Rachel Kaplan would say, these micro doses of nature.
sentences.zh: 它也能给在医院工作的人带来好处，正如蕾切尔·卡普兰所说，这或许能为他们提供这些“微剂量的自然”。

sentences.en: They could give them these little boosts of directed attention.
sentences.zh: 它们可以为他们提供定向注意力的短暂提升。

sentences.en: Very often when we're trying to get somewhere, we focus on getting from point A to point B as quickly and efficiently as possible.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，当我们试图去某个地方时，我们的重点是如何以最快、最高效的方式从A点到达B点。

sentences.en: Mark, you say that we should be asking how green our route can be.
sentences.zh: 马克，你却说我们应该问问我们的路线可以有多绿。

sentences.en: And in fact, you're exploring the development of an app to help people identify the most nature-filled way to walk somewhere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你正在探索开发一款应用程序，帮助人们找出步行前往某地时绿意最浓的路线。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is work that I've done in collaboration with one of my former students, Kate Schertz, where we developed this app called Retune.
sentences.zh: 这是我与我以前的学生凯特·舍茨合作开展的工作，我们开发了一款名为Retune的应用。

sentences.en: So, restoring through urban nature experiences.
sentences.zh: 也就是：通过城市自然体验恢复精力。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you go on Google Maps, it's going to route you on the shortest or most efficient path between point A to point B.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你打开谷歌地图，它会为你规划从A点到B点最短或最高效的路线。

sentences.en: But what we try to do with Retune is try to map people on the walking route that will increase their nature exposure.
sentences.zh: 但我们用Retune试图做的是，为人们规划能增加其自然接触的步行路线。

sentences.en: So, that would increase the number of trees that they would be exposed to, reduce the amount of noise that they would be exposed to.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这会增加他们接触到的树木数量，减少他们接触到的噪音。

sentences.en: And so, what happens with this app is that the path that it might suggest for you might be a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 所以，这款应用带来的结果是，它为你推荐的路径可能会稍微长一点。

sentences.en: But you would be exposed to, you know, more of this softly fascinating natural stimulation that we think would boost cognitive abilities.
sentences.zh: 但你会接触到更多这种温和吸引人的自然刺激，我们认为这可以提升认知能力。

sentences.en: Mark, you found yourself inspired by certain buildings that incorporate elements of nature.
sentences.zh: 马克，你发现自己受到某些融入了自然元素的建筑的启发。

sentences.en: Talk about this, how architecture in some ways can itself be a way of bringing nature indoors.
sentences.zh: 聊聊这个吧，建筑在某些方面本身如何能成为一种将自然引入室内的方式？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really interesting to think about how some of these nature results also might relate to architecture.
sentences.zh: 对，思考其中一些自然成果如何与建筑产生关联，是一件非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, one thing, I don't know if you've ever been to the campus of the University of Chicago, but it's a very beautiful campus,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我不知道你有没有去过芝加哥大学的校园，那是一个非常美丽的校园，

sentences.en: in part because the buildings are just beautiful.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于那些建筑本身就很美。

sentences.en: There's these beautiful Gothic architecture buildings that actually mimic a lot of the patterns in nature.
sentences.zh: 那里有美丽的哥特式建筑，实际上模仿了自然界中的许多图案。

sentences.en: There's a lot of intricacy to the buildings.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑有许多错综复杂的细节。

sentences.en: They have some of the same fractal or scale-free components that real nature has.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有与真实大自然相同的分形或无标度组件。

sentences.en: They have a lot of the curved edge structure that real nature has.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有许多真实自然所具备的曲线边缘结构。

sentences.en: And it just feels like it's possible that it might be having some cognitive benefits to us.
sentences.zh: 这让人觉得，它很有可能对我们的认知产生一些益处。

sentences.en: And I had an architecture student, Alex Coburn, contact me where he was interested in seeing if buildings, building facades or building interiors, if they mimic patterns in nature,
sentences.zh: 曾有一位建筑系学生亚历克斯·科本联系我，他很有兴趣了解建筑、建筑立面或建筑内部如果模仿自然界的图案，

sentences.en: did they also yield some benefits?
sentences.zh: 是否也能带来一些益处？

sentences.en: So he and I, and a few other people, designed some studies where we had people look at different architectural facades.
sentences.zh: 于是他、我和其他几个人设计了一些研究，让人们观察不同的建筑立面。

sentences.en: You know, these would be buildings for hospitals or religious buildings or government buildings.
